// Room "P5 attic south bedroom" (interior designer's part): one bed against the west wall (head on x84, the wall at
// x83), a two-barrel dresser beside its foot, a chest at the east end, a rug down the middle lane, and two standing
// lanterns on the barrel and chest tops as the light. The door (90,6..7,18) opens onto (90,6,19), which stays clear;
// the flue at x88 z18 is in the partition, outside this box.
import { layers, bed } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

export function build(g) {
  // the bed: foot at (85,6,19), head at (84,6,19), against the west wall
  bed(g, [85, 6, 19], "west", "red");

  // origin (84,6,19): rows along +x (x84..91), successive rows along +z (z19, z20); layer y6 then layer y7
  layers(g, [84, 6, 19], {
    "c": ["chest", { facing: "west", type: "single" }],
    "b": ["barrel", { facing: "up", open: "false" }],
    "r": "red_carpet",
    "l": ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
    "f": "flower_pot",
  }, [
    [
      "....rr..", // y6, z19: rug in the middle lane; bed foot and head are placed by bed()
      "bb.....c", // y6, z20: barrels under the bed's foot, chest at the east end
    ],
    [
      "........", // y7, z19: kept clear above the bed
      "lf.....l", // y7, z20: lantern on the barrel, flower pot, lantern on the chest
    ],
  ]);
}

./make.sh exits 0 and writes build.nbt (11527 cells).
left: The room header comment still says the flue at x88 z18 is outside this box, but 88,6,19 is chimney masonry inside it (z19). The header should be corrected by whoever owns the room or the plan.
The rug is now two cells (x86-87, z19) rather than the original two-cell rug at x88-89; the designer may want to re-lay it once the chimney footprint is confirmed in plan.md.

waste.what: Finding which earlier part owned the refused cell (88,6,19) and why: I had to read the make log, parts-report.json and the plan's chimney footprint by hand to learn it was chimney masonry (bricks) at z19, which the room header comment didn't expect.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls, 2 full make.sh runs
waste.tool: A make.sh/runParts report line that names the owning part and the plan box for each refused cell (e.g. 'refused 88,6,19 red_carpet: owned by chimneys (P5 chimney box x87..89 z17..19)'), plus a `layers()` dry-run that checks a legend's cells against the built grid before it writes.

waste.what: Checking that every block id in the part is in palette.json and valid for 1.21.1, by reading palette.json and running `blocks --check` against each id separately.
waste.cost: 2 Bash checks plus one node one-liner over palette.json
waste.tool: `mcd blocks --check <ids> --version 1.21.1` run against the palette file (or a `mcd palette-check part.mjs` that reads the layers legend and bed() calls directly); the default --version was 26.3, which would have misled a check that didn't pass the version.

waste.what: Working out the new rug row by hand: confirming x86-87 at y6 z19 was air and not on the door or bed lane.
waste.cost: one rebuild, plus reading the room's box and door cells from the plan
waste.tool: `mcd plan build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only 'P5 attic south bedroom'` prints the floor grid with occupied cells as 'o', so the free cells can be read off in one call.
